subject: Request to convert temporary buffer into committed capacity + pro-rata credit
snippet: Quick note — can we convert the temporary buffer FreshCart used during launch into a committed block and apply a pro-rata credit for what we've already consumed?
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@freshcart.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Temporary buffer conversion and credits

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for spinning up the temporary buffer last week — it made launch day much less stressful. We consumed roughly 560k tokens over the emergency window (report attached). We're looking to convert that temporary headroom into a short-term committed block or some other arrangement so that: 1) our rate limits reflect the new required QPS for production, and 2) we get a pro-rata credit for the portion already used while we work through procurement.

Questions:
- Can the temporary buffer be converted to a 3-month committed block that starts retroactively from Aug 19th?
- If so, what would the credit look like (line-item on next invoice or separate credit note)?
- Can we get a short-term, 2x rate-limit upgrade for the first 72 hours after conversion to ensure no throttling while we finish the rollout?

I've attached a short consumption report and the draft SOW procurement will use. Procurement is slow; if we can convert now and bill/settle later that would be ideal.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Infrastructure, FreshCart
samir@freshcart.com

Attachments: consumption-report-Jun-2026.csv, FreshCart-SOW-draft.pdf

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@freshcart.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-22T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Temporary buffer conversion and credits

Samir — thanks for the clear note and the reports. High level: we can do two safe paths and I laid out the tradeoffs below so procurement has options.

Option A — Retro-convert to a 3-month commit (recommended if you expect sustained traffic):
- Convert the temporary buffer into a 3-month committed capacity starting 2026-08-19.
- We apply a pro-rata credit equal to the difference between the pay-as-you-go token charges you incurred during the buffer window and the committed rate you would have paid for that volume; credit shows as a line-item on the following invoice.
- Immediate 2x soft rate-limit bump for 72 hours while the SOW/PO is finalized (no extra cost).

Option B — Short-term headroom + staged commit:
- Convert to a 4-week paid headroom block, then convert to a commit at the end of the month if you sign the SOW.
- Smaller upfront payment, but fewer retro credits and slightly higher unit price.

A few notes/asks:
- Ben, can you confirm the mechanics for applying the credit and whether we can cap retro credits to one invoice period?
- Samir, if procurement can share the expected PO date we can align the billing cycle to minimize reconciliation noise.

If this looks good I'll draft the amendment and a one-page summary for Contracts. Happy to jump on a 30-min call today or tomorrow.

Best,
Olga
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com

> Attachment: FreshCart-SOW-draft.pdf

From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@freshcart.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-23T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Temporary buffer conversion and credits — billing treatment

Samir / Olga — quick note on billing mechanics so expectations match:

- Credit calculation: we compute the committed-unit price for the volume consumed during the emergency window and subtract what FreshCart was invoiced under PAYG for those tokens. The delta becomes a credit.
- Application: the credit posts to the next invoice as a negative line item by default. If FreshCart prefers a separate credit note, we can issue one (procurement sometimes requires that).
- Caps: standard practice is to cap retroactive credits to one invoice period unless explicitly agreed otherwise. If you need the credit split across invoices we can accommodate, but it requires Finance sign-off.
- Rate-limit upgrade: we can schedule the 2x soft bump immediately; we'll log a temporary policy so it auto-reverts after 72 hours unless you request an extension.

I've attached a pro-forma showing the sample math for Jul/Aug usage. If you give a green light I'll prepare the amendment and a billing addendum.

Ben Carter
Senior Billing Ops — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: proforma-invoice-Jul-Aug.pdf

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@freshcart.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-24T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Temporary buffer conversion and credits — next steps

Samir — thanks for surfacing this. Proposed next steps:
1) Sign amendment (I will send a DocuSign with Option A terms, 3-month commit starting Aug 19).
2) We apply the pro-rata credit to the next invoice (Ben will post the line-item).
3) Procurement signs the SOW/PO (I've attached the HubSpot deal for reference).

As an incentive to close quickly, we can extend a one-time pilot discount of 10% on the committed unit price if you commit >= 1.5M tokens/month for the 3-month term. This is time-limited to agreements signed by Aug 30.

I'll drop the DocuSign link in the thread shortly. If procurement needs a vendor W-9 or additional paperwork please point them to contracts@redwood.com.

Thanks — Aditya
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8471

From: Samir Khan <samir@freshcart.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@freshcart.com, contracts@freshcart.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-26T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Temporary buffer conversion and credits — acceptance with two asks

All — we appreciate the quick turnaround and the incentive. We will proceed with Option A (3-month commit starting Aug 19) provided two items are clarified in the DocuSign amendment:
1) Explicit language that the 2x soft rate-limit upgrade will be active within 2 hours of sign and will remain for 72 hours unless FreshCart requests an extension.
2) The pro-rata credit should be visible as a separate credit note (Contracts prefers that) rather than only as a negative line item.

Procurement: FYI I'm attaching the SOW they asked for; procurement will route the PO after DocuSign.

Assuming those two items are included, FreshCart will sign the DocuSign within 24 hours of the updated amendment.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Infrastructure, FreshCart

Attachments: FreshCart-SOW-draft.pdf (final), consumption-report-Jun-2026.csv
